review_status: revised-native-pass-complete; acceptable as explicitly estimated exterior candidate

initial_findings.finding: Three near-identical, equal-height stacked balcony/colonnade levels dominate the rendered facade. The source photograph instead shows a much taller deep lower colonnade and a noticeably shorter upper gallery band. This is a recognizable form discrepancy, even though exact storey mapping is unverified.
initial_findings.suggestion: Remove the intermediate repeated gallery beam/slab/railing that cuts the tall lower open volume; preserve a taller lower column run and a shorter upper gallery. Treat exact elevations as design estimates.

initial_findings.finding: The render uses circular stone rings on flat rectangular tower faces. The photo has strong raised arched stone crowns immediately above both visible clock dials, with substantial stone shoulders.
initial_findings.suggestion: Add a simplified curved stone crown and short side shoulders around each observed dial, retaining the separate open lantern above.

initial_findings.finding: The rendered rear and sides are uniform regular window grids. The single source photo does not validate these unseen elevations.
initial_findings.suggestion: Keep regular rear/side fenestration explicitly labeled an estimated continuation.

positive_observations: One principal tower, a lower elongated body and separate rear pitched red roof are present.
Gallery spaces and upper lantern visibly have depth/openings rather than closed flat painted panels.
Two roofed lower pavilion breaks and a far end pavilion provide the major divisions of the long facade.
No obvious floating detached masses, large missing surfaces or severe unintended component penetration appeared in the three initial native images.
limits: This is an exterior form review, not a geometric topology or performance test.
53 m tower height is a chosen secondary documentary anchor with unverified endpoints.
104 m main-body length, 20 m core depth, about 27 m total depth, individual levels and all bay/column counts are design estimates.
Two clock dials are observed in the source photograph; clock graphics and displayed time remain simplified invented presentation details.
Small side-tower identity, original1934 condition, later museum alterations and 2026 condition are not resolved.
No photographic metric calibration, accepted full historic footprint, geographic registration or full listed-site acceptance.

acceptance.basis: Actual viewing of revised front, oblique and rear native renders against the actually viewed 2013 source photo; recognizable exterior forms only.

initial_native_images_note: Hashes below identify the first reviewed render set before correction; files have since been overwritten by native_images above.

resolved_findings.resolution: Revised front and oblique show a tall continuous lower column order with the intervening outer slab/beam/railing removed, and a distinct shorter upper gallery with finer reddish columns. This now follows the visible high/low rhythm of the source photo.
Simplified arched crowns/shoulders are visible above the two dials in the revised oblique view. Their relief and ornament are simplified, while the distinguishing arc is present.

final_observations: Front and oblique retain one principal tower attached to the lower elongated main body, with the facade divided by projecting lower pavilions.

The revised long galleries read as deep open space beneath tall pale columns, with a separate shorter upper gallery and solid terrace parapet. This is materially closer to the source photo than the initial repeated-balcony treatment.
Revised oblique exposes both modeled clock dials, their simplified curved stone crowns, longer recessed tower windows and the open lantern under a red hipped cap.
The long pitched rear red roof remains distinct from the flat terrace in front; it does not incorrectly cover the entire gallery depth.
The rear render is complete as a deliberately simplified continuation but does not acquire source-photo validation from this review.
No obvious floating mass, large missing exterior surface, severe accidental intersection or unsupported detached roof piece was visible in the final front, oblique and rear renders.
Foreground ICBC, the detached right red-roof block, the large white theatre behind and surrounding city masses are absent, consistent with the bounded candidate scope.
remaining_simplifications: Tower and main-body metric proportions, lantern height and exact roof slope are design choices; no calibrated camera or metric photo comparison was performed.
Clock frames, carved stone relief, clock digits/mechanism, pilaster capitals and lower entrance details are simplified.
The source-photo projecting pavilions have more varied detailed facade articulation than the regular window stacks in the candidate.
The main tower lower shoulder and cornice/balustrade detail are simplified; gallery baluster counts and column spacing remain estimated.
Unseen rear/side wall openings, exact corner connections and roof intersections remain estimated.
The small circular feature visible on the lower central/right pavilion is omitted and not accepted as a fully identified secondary clock-tower reconstruction.
Period-specific 2013 roof terrace pergolas, coverings, equipment and vegetation were omitted; no unaltered 1934 or current 2026 condition is claimed.
decision: No further obvious form defect requiring a block of this bounded exterior candidate was found after the gallery and clock-crown corrections. Publication must retain the documented source/period/estimate limits.
